title: Compatibility Result
description: The machine-readable verdict produced when a candidate contract set is compared against a baseline. Published as the compatibility summary a release carries, so the platform gate can decide without re-deriving the comparison. Findings are grouped by what can be proven: breaking changes are demonstrated, review-required changes are those that cannot be shown safe, and compatible changes are proven harmless.

baseline.title: Baseline reference
baseline.description: The released version or ref the candidate was compared against. Null when no prior release exists, in which case 'result' is 'no-baseline' and no comparison was performed.

candidate.title: Candidate reference
candidate.description: The version or ref being evaluated.

result.title: Verdict
result.description: pass: no breaking finding, or every breaking finding is covered by an approved major-version transition. fail: at least one unapproved breaking finding. review_required: no breaking finding, but at least one change that cannot be shown safe. no-baseline: nothing to compare against; the engine was not exercised and this must not be read as a compatibility guarantee.

breaking.title: Breaking findings
breaking.description: Changes demonstrated to reject data or usage that the baseline accepted. A non-empty list fails the gate unless 'approved_major_transition' is true.

review_required.title: Review-required findings
review_required.description: Changes that are additive or undecidable, and therefore cannot be shown safe. Enum expansion and new variants belong here: they are additive yet can break a consumer that matches exhaustively. These block automatic approval until the contract owner records a decision.

compatible.title: Compatible findings
compatible.description: Changes proven not to affect existing consumers.

approved_major_transition.title: Major transition approved
approved_major_transition.description: Whether every breaking finding is covered by a MAJOR version increase on its contract. When true, breaking findings remain listed but do not fail the gate: they were declared, not hidden.

checked_at_utc.title: Check timestamp
checked_at_utc.description: When the comparison ran, as an RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with a literal 'Z' offset.

finding.title: Finding
finding.description: One classified difference between baseline and candidate.

contract_id.title: Affected contract
contract_id.description: URN of the contract the change was found in.

change.title: Change class
change.description: The kind of difference detected. A stable identifier consumers and the platform gate may branch on.

location.title: Location
location.description: JSON pointer to the affected node within the contract, or '#' for a whole-contract change.

detail.title: Explanation
detail.description: Human-readable account of the difference. Not a compatibility key.

witness.title: Proof value
witness.description: A value the baseline accepted and the candidate rejects. Present when a finding was proven by counter-example rather than by structure, which is how an undecidable change such as a regex tightening earns a breaking verdict instead of review_required.

compatible.detail: optional property added; existing consumers are unaffected
